rows: Entry post at ASI: Assistant Archaeologist
150 posts for 2026, subject to change with workload. Pay Level 6.

ASI archaeology cadre, filled versus empty
191 vacant out of 420 sanctioned. Conservation cadre: 447 vacant out of 831.
Lok Sabha written reply, reported by ThePrint on 4 August 2026.
Next rung: Deputy Superintending Archaeologist
67 posts advertised in 2024. 1,407 applied, 293 shortlisted. About 75 of 120 sanctioned posts unfilled.
ThePrint, 14 July 2026. The advertisement is in court, with serving staff arguing the posts belong to internal promotion.
UGC NET June 2026, Archaeology (subject 067), unreserved category
JRF cut-off 212 marks (3 candidates). Assistant Professor cut-off 184 (53). PhD-only cut-off 162 (108).
NTA subject-wise cut-off list, June 2026 session.
Excavation permissions issued by ASI
121 over five years: 24, 31, 19, 22 and 25 (the last three are calendar years).
Lok Sabha reply as reported on 22 July 2026 (a news summary of the reply).
ASI spend on its ongoing excavations
About Rs 6.8 crore so far across 16 ongoing excavations. Highest: Rakhigarhi, Rs 2.16 crore.
ThePrint analysis of a Lok Sabha reply, 20 July 2026.
Entry post at ASI: Assistant Archaeologist
The main central entry door is a few hundred posts at most in any cycle. This is a draft, so read the final rules.
ASI archaeology cadre, filled versus empty
Posts exist and are empty. An empty post is not the same as a hiring drive, because rules, court cases and budgets decide when it is filled.
Next rung: Deputy Superintending Archaeologist
Getting in is one competition. Moving up is a second, slower queue that is stuck in litigation.
UGC NET June 2026, Archaeology (subject 067), unreserved category
The national pool of qualifiers in this subject is tiny, and a funded JRF is rarer still.
Excavation permissions issued by ASI
Roughly 20 to 30 new digs a year for the whole country. Dig-funded jobs are few and short.
ASI spend on its ongoing excavations
Field budgets are small. A project hires a handful of people for a season or a year.

blocks.heading: Rated By How Far They Scale
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Ten routes, rated by how far they scale

rows: GIS, remote sensing and 3D documentation skills (QGIS, drone photogrammetry, LiDAR processing)
Scalable
One skill sells to survey teams, monument owners, mapping and infrastructure clients outside heritage too. You set the project price and can add people.
Heritage documentation and conservation-planning consultancy (monument surveys, heritage impact reports, CSR heritage projects)
Scalable with a business layer
Owners, trusts, developers near protected monuments and CSR funders need documents they cannot write themselves. Repeat clients are possible.
Archaeological science (archaeobotany, isotope and residue work, dating, ancient DNA)
Scalable with a business layer
A scarce skill. An archaeobotanist at the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences says ASI relies largely on outside institutions to check samples.
Conservation and museum work (objects, condition reports, collections)
Scalable with a business layer
Conservators who can treat objects and write condition reports can serve trusts, private collectors and corporate museums as well as public ones.
Heritage tourism: guiding, heritage walks, story-led trips
Scalable with a business layer
People pay you directly, reviews build trust, and you can add guides and routes. This is the one route where the customer is a person, not an institution.
Contract research on a university or institute excavation project
Not so scalable
A post funds one project for one year at a time. A 2026 IIT Gandhinagar project assistant post paid Rs 28,000 to Rs 44,000 a month for one year, with fieldwork.
GIS, remote sensing and 3D documentation skills (QGIS, drone photogrammetry, LiDAR processing)

Heritage clients are few and slow to pay, so the portable skill is what keeps you employable. A vendor case study described a pilot LiDAR scan of a Telangana temple done under ASI supervision, so public work exists but is still at pilot scale.
Heritage documentation and conservation-planning consultancy (monument surveys, heritage impact reports, CSR heritage projects)
A registered firm, a written scope, and a partner such as a conservation architect. We found no public income data, so start as a partner, not alone.
Archaeological science (archaeobotany, isotope and residue work, dating, ancient DNA)
Analysis services and joint projects are the layer. The paying market is small and mostly public money. You need a science degree such as botany, zoology, chemistry or geology.
Conservation and museum work (objects, condition reports, collections)
A small conservation studio. Salaried museum posts are modest, and a 2021 parliamentary committee found museums often understaffed.
Heritage tourism: guiding, heritage walks, story-led trips
Guide licence rules and seasonal demand. The history guide on this site covers the Ministry of Tourism certification.
Contract research on a university or institute excavation project
Use one or two project years as proof, and add a GIS or science skill before the funding ends.
Post and pay
Assistant Archaeologist, Group B non-gazetted. Pay Level 6 in the pay matrix, Rs 35,400 to Rs 1,12,400. That is the basic pay band, before allowances.
Number of posts
150 for 2026, with a note that the number can vary with workload.
Qualification

A master's degree in Archaeology, or in Ancient Indian History, Culture and Archaeology, or in Ancient or Medieval Indian History with at least two of: Field Archaeology, Art and Architecture, Epigraphy, Numismatics. The degree must be from a recognised university.
Age limit

Not above 30 for direct recruits, with up to five years more for government servants and other relaxations under central rules. The cut-off date follows the advertisement of the Staff Selection Commission.
Probation and training
Two years of probation, which includes six months of in-service field training in archaeology.
How it is filled
Direct recruitment. Short vacancies caused by leave or deputation can be filled by deputation from central government staff.

blocks.heading: Study, and What to Check First
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Where to study, and what to check first

rows: ASI's own institute (Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, Greater Noida)

A PG Diploma in Archaeology. The ASI page says the process starts in July to August each year. Older notices asked for a master's degree in a related subject with 55% marks, an entrance test and an interview.

The older notice may be out of date. Ask about current faculty, intake and the entry rule, because news reports in 2026 described 15 students and no permanent faculty. ThePrint also reported the diploma being cut from two years to one.
Deccan College, Pune

MA in Ancient Indian History, Culture and Archaeology, PhD, a PG Diploma in Museology, a Diploma in Heritage Sites Management and Scientific Conservation, and a PG Diploma in Underwater Archaeology that its page lists as one year with weekend classes.
The department page lists an entrance test syllabus. Some diploma pages carry old dates and conflicting fees, so email the institute for the current fee and intake.
Banaras Hindu University
MA in Ancient Indian History, Culture and Archaeology. Listings say admission runs through CUET PG on the Samarth portal.
Seat counts conflict across listing sites (28 in one, 77 in another). Read the official brochure.
JNU, Centre for Historical Studies
Archaeology is taught inside the ancient history stream. Course lists show early South Asian archaeology and historical archaeology courses.
Read the current admission notice for the MA and research programmes before you plan around it.
National Museum Institute, Delhi
History of Art, Conservation and Museology programmes, the usual door to curator and conservation posts.
Listing sites disagree on the entry process (own test and interview, or merit). Use nmi.gov.in.
Indian Institute of Heritage (planned)
Announced in 2023 as a deemed university at Noida that would absorb the ASI institute, the National Museum Institute and others.
We found no admission details. Do not plan around it until it takes students.

rows: Assistant Archaeologist (ASI, central)
Pay Level 6: Rs 35,400 to Rs 1,12,400 basic band, before allowances.
ASI draft recruitment rules, 20 April 2026. Final rules may differ.
Project assistant on a university research project
Rs 28,000 to Rs 44,000 a month, consolidated, for one year.
One IIT Gandhinagar listing (Vadnagar glass project), 2026. One project, not a market average.
Entry pay quoted by career portals
From about Rs 2.5 lakh to Rs 12 lakh a year, depending on the portal.
Collegedunia, CorpReady and Careers360 answers. They disagree with each other and are not official, so we do not use them as a guide.
Consulting, documentation, conservation studio or guide income
No reliable public figure found.
We print none. Ask three people working in your city what they earned in year one, and how many months had no paid work.

Finding possible sites in LiDAR and satellite data
Medium

A 2025 study that searched for hillforts across England, Hesse and Molise got F1 scores of 34% to 38%, and concluded that people must check false positives. A tool called ADAF aims to help archaeologists with no machine-learning background.
3D recording with photogrammetry and laser scanning
High for routine capture
Cameras, drones and software make capture cheaper and faster. A 2024 preprint on a temple gateway in Karnataka combined drone and ground photogrammetry with laser scanning.
Reading a trench, telling layers apart, deciding where to dig
Low
Physical, local and judgment-heavy work.
Finding possible sites in LiDAR and satellite data
Fieldwalking, test pits and the judgment of what a feature is.
QGIS and basic remote sensing. Always check the output on the ground.
3D recording with photogrammetry and laser scanning
Choosing what to record, scale control, permissions and interpretation.
Capture discipline: overlap, lighting, control points. Free tools such as QGIS and open photogrammetry software let you practise.
First drafts of reports, catalogues and labels
Context, accuracy and responsibility. A wrong layer number in a report is your mistake, not the tool's.
Use AI for a first draft and check every fact against your field notes.
Reading a trench, telling layers apart, deciding where to dig
All of it.
Time in the field with a good supervisor.
Permissions, site communities, funders
All of it.
Plain English writing and calm, specific follow-up.
You need a steady income soon after your degree
Entry posts are few, advertisements are irregular and project jobs run for a year at a time. Start with a skill that pays elsewhere while you build archaeology proof.
You picture finds and discoveries more than recording
Most of the work is measuring, drawing, labelling and report writing. Visit a dig or a museum store room before you commit.
You want to borrow money for a private diploma or a high-fee course
No private certificate replaces the public MA and the exam route. Avoid education debt for this field.
You cannot spend time outdoors or away from home
Lab, museum and digital routes exist, but they still need field knowledge. Pick them on purpose.
You expect a government post to follow your degree
A degree is the ticket to apply, not a promise. Many posts are empty and are not being filled on a fixed schedule.
You dislike writing and follow-up
Reports, proposals and permission letters are a big part of the job at every level.
Class 12 student

Choose a BA that includes ancient history or archaeology through CUET and keep your major flexible. Also build one skill that sells elsewhere (maps, photography, writing). Try a dig visit or museum volunteering before you commit.
History or arts graduate

Read the ASI draft rules. If you want that route, check that your MA includes the required subjects, and note the age limit. Read the history guide on this site to compare the other doors for a history graduate.
Science graduate (botany, zoology, chemistry, geology)
Your science degree is a real advantage in archaeological science, where labs are thin. Look for a project that needs sampling or analysis, and learn how excavation teams record context.
Working professional or career changer

Try one weekend course or museum volunteering first. A Deccan College diploma can be taken alongside a job per its page, but confirm the current rules. Do not resign until you have a paid project or a firm offer.
